Identity guard: erythroplasia of Queyrat is itself squamous cell carcinoma in situ, so the edge asserts an association between an in-situ lesion identity and the invasive SCC identity, not a normal-tissue-to-cancer pathway; progression and coexistence figures are PeIN-population scoped.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 31 (2026-09-23): one bounded squamous-cell-carcinoma association authored under the established pre-malignant-identity precedent (bowen-s-disease -> SCC and actinic-keratosis -> SCC are already carried as ASSOCIATION_ONLY) - the Kravvas 2022 345-patient PeIN series documents concomitant invasive penile SCC at presentation in 8.7% and progression in 2.6%, and the Proietti 2021 series confirms EQ as SCC in situ; the in-situ-identity and PeIN-population-scope guards are recorded on the edge.

No penile-cancer-specific catalog identity exists (skin-cancer is melanoma/non-melanoma-scoped and is sun-exposure anchored, while SCC is the penile-lesion-histology target used by the lichen-sclerosus and bowen's-disease precedents), so this edge follows the squamous-cell-carcinoma target rather than inventing a new identity.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: In the largest PeIN series (345 patients, Kravvas 2022), 8.7% had concomitant invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma at presentation and 2.6% progressed to invasive SCC during follow-up, and the Proietti 2021 series reiterates that erythroplasia of Queyrat is squamous cell carcinoma in situ of the glans with invasive potential; population series place progression risk broadly in the low single digits to one-third range depending on duration and treatment.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert a normal-tissue carcinogenesis pathway: EQ is SCC in situ, so the relationship is the in-situ-to-invasive identity transition of the same neoplasm; individual claims require biopsy-proven in-situ disease at baseline, histologic confirmation of invasion, and exclusion of de novo invasive carcinoma; the coexistence figures are PeIN-population scoped and cannot establish individual progression timing.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized in-situ-to-invasive progression pathway: the same HPV-driven or lichen-sclerosus-associated keratinocyte dysplasia that constitutes erythroplasia of Queyrat acquires invasive capability when malignant cells breach the basement membrane, converting in-situ carcinoma into invasive penile SCC with metastatic potential; the pathway is the accepted biology of in-situ lesions and requires no extrapolation, but individual progression timing is not predictable from population series.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association between the in-situ identity and the invasive identity of the same neoplasm: population figures are PeIN-scoped rather than EQ-specific, progression timing is not individually predictable, HPV and lichen-sclerosus co-drivers must be documented, and biopsy of any suspicious area is required rather than assumed; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Biopsy-proven erythroplasia of Queyrat (SCC in situ) with HPV and lichen-sclerosus status documented; histologic confirmation of invasion for any suspected progression; surveillance history and interval chronology; exclusion of de novo invasive carcinoma arising outside the in-situ field; dermatology and urology assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: De novo invasive penile SCC unrelated to the in-situ field
Zoon's plasma cell balanitis or inflammatory mimics misdiagnosed as EQ
Melanoma or other non-squamous penile malignancy
Metastatic disease to the penis from another primary

evidenceGaps: Biopsy-proven erythroplasia of Queyrat (SCC in situ) with HPV and lichen-sclerosus status documented; histologic confirmation of invasion for any suspected progression; surveillance history and interval chronology; exclusion of de novo invasive carcinoma arising outside the in-situ field; dermatology and urology assessment of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY following the bowen's-disease and actinic-keratosis precedents: the in-situ-to-invasive relationship is documented in the largest PeIN series, but the mapping asserts the association and not an individual progression claim; no causation or probability is forced.
